name: Question 6
problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $10$-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+5$ defined on $[-5,5).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $10$-periodic extension of $G(x)=-\frac{3}{2}x$ from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+5∼-\frac{5}{4}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{75(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f$ is 
{{field-2}}
and
{{field-3}}
on $R,$ we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
-\frac{3}{2}x∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-4}}\cdot {{field-5}}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=5$ and we are already given the coefficients ${a}_{0}$ and ${a}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼-\frac{5}{4}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{75(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5}).
$$

Now, notice that 

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-5,5),$

- continuous on $[-5,5),$ and

- satisfies $F(-5)=F(5),$ if we extend the value at $x=5$ using the formula $F(x)=-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+5.$

Therefore, the $10$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{continuous}$ and $\text{piecewise smooth}$ on $R,$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}+5) & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{5}{4})+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{75(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5})) \\ -\frac{3}{2}x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{75(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5})) \\ -\frac{3}{2}x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-15(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5}) \\ -\frac{3}{2}x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{15(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5})\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, notice that F(x) is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its 2L-periodic extension has the form a02+∑n=1∞ancos⁡(nπxL).

In our case, L=5 and we are already given the coefficients a0 and an for n≥1. Thus, the Fourier series of f(x) is given by f(x)∼−54+∑n=1∞75(−1)n+1n2π2cos⁡(nπx5).

Now, notice that

  • the function F is continuously differentiable on (−5,5),

  • continuous on [−5,5), and

  • satisfies F(−5)=F(5), if we extend the value at x=5 using the formula F(x)=−34x2+5.

Therefore, the 10-periodic extension f is continuous and piecewise smooth on R, so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

ddx(−34x2+5)∼ddx(−54)+∑n=1∞ddx(75(−1)n+1n2π2cos⁡(nπx5))−32x∼0+∑n=1∞75(−1)n+1n2π2⋅(−nπ5sin⁡(nπx5))−32x∼∑n=1∞−15(−1)n+1nπsin⁡(nπx5)−32x∼∑n=1∞15(−1)nnπ⋅sin⁡(nπx5)
